requirements.requirement: Run a healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application data
requirements.summary: After building the cluster from bare hosts, direct queries show wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, and all three nodes Synced. The appdb.orders table with 5 rows is confirmed present identically on node1, node2, and node3.

requirements.requirement: Bring the entire cluster down completely for a maintenance window
requirements.summary: A durability-proving write (6th row, sum 2093.39) was committed before shutdown. mariadb was stopped cleanly on node3, then node2, then node1, with grastate.dat seqno captured on each (13/14/15, node1 highest with safe_to_bootstrap=1). Subsequent systemctl is-active checks on all three nodes simultaneously returned inactive (exit 3), directly confirming the whole cluster was down.

requirements.requirement: Bring the cluster back up after the maintenance window with every committed write still present
requirements.summary: node1 (highest seqno) was bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster and immediately showed all 6 rows / sum 2093.39. After node2 and node3 rejoined via IST, the same 6 rows and sum were independently confirmed on node2 and node3, matching the pre-shutdown state exactly.

requirements.requirement: All three members serving again after the maintenance window
requirements.summary: Post-recovery check on node1 shows wsrep_cluster_size=3 and wsrep_cluster_status=Primary; node2 and node3 both individually report wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced alongside identical data, directly confirming all three members were serving.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node (independent of public contract)
requirements.summary: Each node had a pre-restart boot_id baseline, a systemctl reboot acknowledgement, a connection drop/timeout during the transition, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and a recovered cluster/data check (size 3, Synced/Primary, 6 rows sum 2093.39) — done one at a time so the other two nodes preserved quorum. Boot-id values in the command timeline match the fixed after-prepare/after-executor snapshots exactly for all three nodes, providing a coherent independent cross-check.

overall_summary: The executor built a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster from bare AlmaLinux hosts, loaded application data, and directly demonstrated the required lifecycle: a healthy 3/3 Synced baseline, a committed write made just before shutdown, a fully verified complete stop of all three members (grastate seqno-based bootstrap selection), and a full restore with all 6 rows (sum 2093.39) present and all three nodes serving and Synced again. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed on all three nodes one at a time with quorum preserved, showing changed boot identities and full data/cluster recovery, consistent with the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot. Troubleshooting detours (an SST failure requiring a datadir wipe on node2, and iterative SELinux policy fixes for mariadb-backup) were bounded, corrective, and left no damaging residue; only minor leftover temp files remain.
limitations: Command outputs are potentially bounded/truncated by the collector, so some intermediate detail (e.g., full journalctl/audit content) was not fully visible.
No public-contract requirement to clean up temp files, but /tmp residue (install.log, pp.b64, start.log/pid, etc.) was left in place on all three nodes per the after-executor snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command trace. All package installs, firewall port openings (3306/4567/4568/4444 tcp + 4567 udp), bind-address=0.0.0.0, and galera.cnf writes are necessary prerequisites for a Galera cluster on bare hosts with no prior MariaDB and were confirmed present at final state without conflicting services. Two troubleshooting sequences occurred: (1) an SST failure on node2 led to `rm -rf /var/lib/mysql/*` (cmd-eaaee1314dbd4de0) to clear a corrupted datadir before retrying start — a bounded, necessary corrective action directly tied to fixing a failed prior attempt, not residue since the directory was cleanly repopulated by the successful SST. (2) An SELinux AVC block on mariadb-backup was resolved via audit2allow; an initial attempt to reuse a single exported galera_sst.pp policy package on node2/node3 (cmd-1ed0950b3aab453e, cmd-bb06cf797a234deb) failed to install (corrupted module), so a corrected per-node policy was generated and successfully applied (cmd-e964854c80014d97, cmd-30d836dc7bd54755) — a legitimate corrective step with no functional residue since the failed .pp files were never activated. The final after-executor snapshot shows no failed systemd units on any node and no unexpected listening sockets beyond ssh, chronyd, and mariadbd (3306/4567), so no unsafe exposure was introduced. The main hygiene deduction is leftover low-risk temp files (/tmp/install.log, install.pid, pp.b64, galera_sst.pp.b64, start.log, start.pid) not cleaned up on the managed nodes, visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff; these are bounded, non-sensitive artifacts of legitimate install/start operations rather than unnecessary mutations.
